# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 50 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 50 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_050_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 1 — The Two Cities

**50:1** He said to me: "You know that you are a sojourner and alien, and that your own city is far away. If you know your own city in which you are destined to dwell, why do you make preparations here — fields and costly furnishings and buildings and rooms that are superfluous? The one who makes such preparations for this city is unable to return to his own city.

**50:2** You foolish, double-minded, and miserable man — do you not perceive that all these things belong to another and are subject to another's power? For the lord of this city will say to you: I do not wish you to dwell in my city; depart from my city, because you do not observe my laws. You, therefore, who possess fields and dwellings and many possessions — when he expels you, what will you do with your field and your house and all the things you have prepared for yourself?

**50:3** For the lord of this place rightly says to you: either use my laws or depart from my dominion. What then will you do, you who have a law from your own city? Will you, for the sake of your fields and the rest of your possessions, completely renounce your own law and live according to the law of this city? Beware — it may not be advantageous to renounce your own law; for if you wish to return to your own city, you will not be received, because you have renounced the law of your own city and will be shut out of it.

**50:4** Take care, therefore. As a sojourner in a foreign land, make no more provision for yourself beyond what is sufficient for your needs, and hold yourself in readiness, so that when the master of this city wills to expel you for resisting his law, you may depart from his city and go to your own city and employ your own law with all joy, suffering no injury.

**50:5** Take care, therefore, you who serve God and have him in your hearts. Practice the works of God, keeping in mind his commandments and the promises he has made, and trust him to fulfill them if his commandments are kept. Therefore instead of fields, purchase souls that are afflicted, insofar as each one is able, and visit widows and orphans and do not neglect them, and spend your wealth and all your possessions on fields and houses of this kind, which you have received from God.

**50:6** For to this end the Master enriched you, that you might perform these ministrations for him. It is far better to acquire such fields and goods and houses as you will find in your own city when you return to it. This expenditure is noble and sacred, attended by neither grief nor fear, but by joy. Therefore do not practice the expenditure of the Gentiles — for it is unprofitable for you who are servants of God.

**50:7** But practice your own expenditure, in which you can rejoice; and do not counterfeit or touch what belongs to another, nor desire it — for it is evil to desire the possessions of another man. But do your own work and you shall be saved."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the sojourner theology of Similitude 1.*
